goal: In build-implement.js, if any file in a TestSet imports through a relative path that leads outside the TestSet directory, the run is marked invalid. That round's test results then do not count against the implementation. Runs k7, k11 and k13 hit this: tests at .artifacts/tests/<task>/ imported '../../../substrate/test/helpers.js', which loaded the main checkout's pre-task code. The change has three parts. (1) The Test Runner agent (label run:${task.id}:${tag}) reports every relative import/require specifier in the TestSet files. (2) A pure function escapingImports({ tests_ref, imports }), added to the fix-loop decisions sentinel block, decides which of those imports escape. When any do, the escaping files go to the Test Author on the existing testfix: path, the correctness lens is told the run was invalid instead of being given its failures, and the round is recorded in the run output as import_escapes. (3) The tests: prompt in build-implement.js and .claude/agents/test-author.md tell the Test Author four things: never use a relative import that climbs out of the TestSet directory; import repo helpers as './helpers.js', './fixloop-helpers.js' and './extract-fixloop.js', because the TestSet lands beside them in substrate/test/; and a test that starts an in-process HTTP server must drive the CLI with an async child process, never spawnSync.

out_of_scope: Changing lens verdict derivation (normalizeVerdict, adjudicate, lensStreaks) or any judge or tiebreak logic
Changing testValidity or the B6 validity detector's facts or classification
Editing substrate/test/helpers.js, fixloop-helpers.js, extract-fixloop.js or b5-wiring-helpers.js (tests may import them but must not change them)
Having the script itself read files or resolve paths with node modules; the Test Runner agent does the file reading, and escapingImports is pure string logic
Any test that shells out to npm test
Rewriting existing TestSets or tests already in substrate/test/
Changing the integration or merge stage, or where TestSets are landed
risk_reasons: rule: surface ref names a sensitive term: .claude/agents/test-author.md
TestResults schema is extended with an optional imports property (array of {file, specifier} objects); no existing fields are removed or changed. Per the rules, additive schema changes are low risk.
Final run output gains an optional import_escapes array ({round, file, specifier} entries); this is additive to EvidenceBundle with no breaking changes to existing consumers.

The fix-loop decisions sentinel block (lines between '// ---- BEGIN fix-loop decisions ----' and '// ---- END fix-loop decisions ----') gains a new escapingImports function. AC-1 confirms existing decision functions continue to work without error.
Touched surfaces are limited to .claude/workflows/build-implement.js and .claude/agents/test-author.md. AC-12 excludes changes to lens verdict derivation, judges, testValidity, and other workflows.
Test Author routing (testfix path) and correctness lens prompts receive enhanced instructions when escaping imports are detected; these are additive context, not contract breaks.
The change is corrective logic fixing a known gap (detecting TestSets that import outside their directory, as seen in runs k7, k11, k13), not a regression to existing functionality.
